<div class="abstract">

**Background.** Atrophy in neurodegenerative dementias is often said to follow the
connectome, but connectomes and atrophy maps are both organised by distance, and the null
models used to test network effects differ in what they preserve. We asked whether any
structural communication model explains atrophy beyond spatial proximity in Alzheimer's
disease (AD) and frontotemporal dementia (FTD), two cortical diseases with distinct
topographies.

**Methods.** Open group-level deformation-based morphometry maps of AD, MCI, FTD and its
behavioural (bvFTD), semantic (svPPA) and non-fluent (nfvPPA) variants were parcellated into
400 cortical regions (100 and 200 for robustness) and 14 subcortical structures with atlases
nonlinearly registered to the maps' template. We predicted each region's atrophy from all
other regions using the Human Connectome Project structural connectome (direct connections,
shortest paths, communicability, search information, navigation, diffusion), functional
connectivity, generative network diffusion from seeds, and Euclidean and geodesic spatial
kernels, with five null models (spin, variogram-matched, Moran spectral randomisation,
degree- and geometry-preserving rewiring) and all parameters refitted inside every null.

**Results.** A geodesic spatial kernel predicted atrophy best in every syndrome (AD
r = `r f2(rv("ctx400_geo", 0, "distance", "AD"))`, bvFTD r = `r f2(rv("ctx400_geo", 0, "distance", "bvFTD"))`)
and outperformed the Euclidean kernel. No structural communication model exceeded the spatial
baselines or survived the variogram-matched null in any syndrome, including after adding the
subcortex, and seeded network diffusion on the structural connectome was never better than
spatial spread from the same seed. When only regions more than 30 mm away were allowed,
thresholded functional connectivity predicted atrophy in bvFTD
(r = `r f2(rv("ctx400_euc", 30, "FC_top10", "bvFTD"))`) and FTD
(r = `r f2(rv("ctx400_euc", 30, "FC_top10", "FTD"))`) under every null; in AD the unique
long-range functional contribution beyond distance was about half as large (partial
r = `r f2(part("ctx400_geo", 30, "FC_top10", "AD")$partial_r)` vs `r f2(part("ctx400_geo", 30, "FC_top10", "bvFTD")$partial_r)`).
Degree-preserving rewiring supported every structural fit and spins about a third;
variogram-matched surrogates supported none.

**Conclusions.** Cortical atrophy in AD and FTD is organised mainly by proximity along the
cortical sheet; structural communication models add little beyond that geometry. FTD,
particularly bvFTD, additionally follows the long-range functional architecture. Network
claims about atrophy should be tested against fitted spatial baselines and
geometry-preserving nulls.

</div>
